title: The Hedgehog and the Wood Pigeons

keywords: the hedgehog and the wood pigeons
full_text:
Beside an ancient palm grove lived a family of wood pigeons who nested in the crown of a tall date palm. The tree was laden with clusters of sweet, honeyed dates, but the birds dropped many ripe dates upon the grass as they fed. Beneath the roots dwelt a cunning hedgehog whose prickly coat hid a mind steeped in trickery.

Longing to devour all the dates himself, the hedgehog donned an ascetic’s cloak made of woven palm fiber, tied a string of prayer beads around his neck, and sat at the foot of the palm tree with eyes cast down, murmuring prayers and fasting.

The gentle pigeons looked down from their leafy bower and marveled at his apparent holiness. 'Look at our neighbor the hedgehog!' cooed the mother pigeon. 'He has abandoned the pleasures of the world and spends his days in humble devotion. Let us descend and seek his spiritual counsel.'

The elder pigeon descended to the grass, bowed respectfully, and said: 'Peace be upon you, venerable hermit. Will you share with us your pearls of wisdom?'

The hedgehog wiped an imaginary tear and sighed: 'Peace be upon you, noble birds. I have realized that true peace comes only from renouncing earthly stores. He who hoards grain and fruit in high trees lives in constant anxiety. If you wish your souls to be light as the desert breeze, bring down all your dates and pile them at my hermitage, that I may distribute them to the poor and needy creatures of the forest.'

The pious pigeons, touched by his eloquent words, spent the entire day flying up and down, carrying every single ripe date from the treetop and stacking them in a massive mound before the hedgehog's burrow.

As night fell, the hedgehog threw off his prayer beads, kicked aside his ascetic's cloak, and rolled himself over the mound of dates, impaling dozens of the fruit upon his sharp spines! Laughing heartily at the gullible birds, he dragged his prize into his subterranean cave, leaving the cold, hungry pigeons on their bare palm tree to weep over the false piety that had stripped them of their winter food.
moral: Beware of hypocrites who don the cloak of piety merely to strip the innocent of their possessions.

Believing rumors and flattery without proof
